xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3083: Passed+ready issues get re-dispatched for review, knocking them out of the ready queue and invalidating UAT generations

plan.title: Passed+ready issues get re-dispatched for review, knocking them out of the ready queue and invalidating UAT generations
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: needsReviewDispatch (src/lib/review-dispatch-decision.ts:19) never checks reviewStatus === 'passed' or readyForMerge, so a stale durable reviewRequestedAt intent keeps re-dispatching review convoys for issues already passed and queued to merge. Each dispatch knocks the issue out of the ready queue, which invalidates the UAT generation it belongs to (uat-reconciler isStale: 'left the ready queue'), tearing down and rebuilding batches indefinitely while burning a full review convoy per cycle. The regression guard blocks some status writes but not the dispatch — and rejecting the spawn's write also discards the reviewSpawnedAt stamp that would mark the intent serviced, so the loop never converges.
narratives.Proposal: Three-layer fix per the PRD (.pan/drafts/PAN-3083.md): (1) guard the pure predicate — return false on reviewStatus 'passed'/'skipped' and on readyForMerge, passing readyForMerge from maybeAutoDispatchReviewHostSide; (2) consume the intent — when a terminal review verdict lands in setReviewStatusSync, clear a serviced reviewRequestedAt (requestedAt <= spawnedAt, or spawnedAt absent) so it is removed from both the DB row and the journal record, while preserving an unserviced newer request; (3) let sandboxed verdict writes propagate the clear by adding reviewRequestedAt to FALLBACK_CLEARABLE_FIELDS. Genuine re-review still works because both legitimate paths (pan done on a new commit; operator force re-request) reset reviewStatus to 'pending' before writing a fresh intent. Regression tests lock the predicate, the consumption, the fallback clear, and UAT-generation stability.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to the 30s dispatch throttle or dispatchReviewHostSide
- No weakening or modification of the reviewStatus regression guards (review-status.ts:190-214, review-status-json.ts:61)
- No root-cause repair of how PAN-3037's stale intent timestamp was produced (PAN-3076 / polyrepo anchor territory)
- No changes to UAT reconciler invalidation semantics (isStale stays as-is)
- No polyrepo/composite-anchor changes (PAN-3076, PAN-2948)
- No fix for the pre-existing mid-review pan-done race (late verdict overwriting a pending reset)

autoDecisions.summary: Guard both 'passed' and 'skipped' in the predicate
autoDecisions.rationale: skipped is the review-mode-none success verdict and advances the lifecycle exactly like passed; a resurrected newer intent would loop identically on it.

autoDecisions.summary: Consume the intent conditionally (serviced only: requestedAt <= spawnedAt, or spawnedAt absent), on all terminal verdicts
autoDecisions.rationale: Preserves a genuinely newer mid-review request from a new commit; when spawnedAt is missing the verdict itself proves the request was serviced. Any terminal verdict (passed/blocked/failed/skipped) services the request that produced its cycle.

autoDecisions.summary: No verdict-timestamp parameter added to the predicate
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's 'unless a newer request postdates the verdict' clause is satisfied structurally: both genuine re-review paths (pan done new-commit path, operator force) reset reviewStatus to 'pending' before writing a fresh intent, so the passed guard never sees them; keeping the predicate's input surface small keeps it pure.

The workspace verdict fallback drain preserves absent keys unless listed in clearedFields; without this a sandboxed verdict write would resurrect the intent from the record and the loop would persist until a host-side write.

autoDecisions.summary: UAT protection is verified at the reconciler level with dependency injection plus the pure predicate, not an end-to-end pipeline test
autoDecisions.rationale: reconcileUatGenerations takes UatReconcilerDeps, making 'member stays in ready set => generation survives' directly assertable; the dispatch side is locked by the pure predicate test on the exact PAN-3037 field snapshot.

items.title: Guard needsReviewDispatch against passed/skipped verdicts and readyForMerge

expected_outputs: tests/unit/lib/review-dispatch-decision.test.ts passes with the PAN-3037 snapshot case asserting no dispatch

narrative.Action: In src/lib/review-dispatch-decision.ts, add `readyForMerge?: boolean` to the params type and two guards before the timestamp comparison: return false when reviewStatus is 'passed' or 'skipped', and return false when readyForMerge is true (exact before/after snippet in .pan/drafts/PAN-3083.md). Extend the doc comment to state that genuine re-review paths reset reviewStatus to 'pending' first (pan done new-commit path at src/cli/commands/done.ts:780-855; operator force at routes/workspaces/review-pipeline.ts:441-504). In src/lib/review-status.ts:510-515 (maybeAutoDispatchReviewHostSide), add `readyForMerge: status.readyForMerge` to the params passed to needsReviewDispatch. Verify (do not change) that the deacon call site src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts:1174 passes the whole status object and therefore picks up the field structurally. Create tests/unit/lib/review-dispatch-decision.test.ts (no test file exists today) covering: the PAN-3037 snapshot ({reviewStatus:'passed', readyForMerge:true, reviewRequestedAt newer than reviewSpawnedAt}) -> false; {reviewStatus:'skipped'} with newer request -> false; {readyForMerge:true, reviewStatus:'pending'} -> false; {reviewStatus:'pending', reviewRequestedAt newer} -> true; missing reviewSpawnedAt with pending -> true; existing 'reviewing' and 'merged' guards -> false; missing reviewRequestedAt -> false. The function must stay pure (no I/O, no new imports).

Terminal review verdict consumes a serviced reviewRequestedAt in setReviewStatusSync

expected_outputs: tests/unit/lib/review-status.test.ts passes including the new consume-on-verdict cases asserting the journal record no longer carries reviewRequestedAt

narrative.Action: In src/lib/review-status.ts setReviewStatusSync, after the `merged` computation (the spread at :227 and the reviewerVerdicts merge at :232-234) and before history tracking, insert the consumption block from the PRD (.pan/drafts/PAN-3083.md, 'Before/after — intent consumption'): when update.reviewStatus transitions into a terminal verdict ('passed'|'blocked'|'failed'|'skipped', different from the prior status) and merged.reviewRequestedAt is set, clear it when serviced — Date.parse(reviewRequestedAt) <= new Date(reviewSpawnedAt).getTime(), or reviewSpawnedAt absent. Preserve it when the request is newer than the spawn (unserviced mid-review request). The clear must be an explicit assignment on `merged` (spread semantics: explicit undefined overrides), so the cleared value flows through normalizeReviewStatusSync into `updated` and then into updateIssueRecordForReviewStatusSync at :321, removing the field from the journal pipeline record (projectPipeline at src/lib/pan-dir/records.ts:126 writes it verbatim; JSON.stringify drops undefined keys). Tests in tests/unit/lib/review-status.test.ts must assert BOTH the returned status and the journal record's pipeline block lack the field after a serviced clear (hazard H1: enrichReviewNotesFromRecordSync:88 resurrects any journal-side leftover on every read), that an unserviced newer request survives, that a missing reviewSpawnedAt still clears, and that non-verdict updates (e.g. a testStatus-only write) never touch the field.

Add reviewRequestedAt to FALLBACK_CLEARABLE_FIELDS so sandboxed verdict writes propagate the clear

No other production change: writeWorkspaceVerdictFallbackSync (:180-182) already lists any clearable field that is undefined on the written status into clearedFields, and the drain honors clearedFields on merge (see the :356 comment). Extend tests/unit/lib/overdeck/review-status-record-sync-fallback.test.ts: (a) a fallback written from a status whose reviewRequestedAt is undefined includes 'reviewRequestedAt' in clearedFields; (b) draining such a fallback removes reviewRequestedAt from the record's pipeline block instead of preserving the prior value; (c) a fallback written from a status that still carries reviewRequestedAt preserves it through the drain. Follow the existing test patterns in that file; if drain-side assertions fit better in review-status-record-sync-drain.test.ts, put them there. Repo rule: any retry/delay in these paths is tested with vi.useFakeTimers().

Regression test: a passed+ready issue with a stale intent does not invalidate its UAT generation

expected_outputs: uat-reconciler.test.ts passes with the new PAN-3083 regression cases (no invalidation when the member stays ready; invalidation when it genuinely departs)

narrative.Action: Add a PAN-3083 regression describe-block to tests/unit/lib/cloister/uat-reconciler.test.ts using the existing UatReconcilerDeps injection pattern. Case 1 (the fix): build a status snapshot {reviewStatus:'passed', testStatus:'passed', readyForMerge:true, reviewRequestedAt newer than reviewSpawnedAt}; assert needsReviewDispatch (imported from src/lib/review-dispatch-decision.js) returns false for it; then run reconcileUatGenerations with a getReadySet that still contains the member (unchanged branch/headSha) against a live generation containing that member, and assert the result invalidates nothing and the generation is not marked stale. Case 2 (test sensitivity lock): the same generation with a getReadySet that omits the member IS invalidated with the 'left the ready queue' reason. This pairs the pure dispatch decision with the reconciler behavior to encode the end-to-end claim of the issue: no spurious dispatch => member never leaves the ready set => generation survives.

items.title: Given a live generation whose member has reviewStatus 'passed', testStatus 'passed', readyForMerge true, and a stale newer reviewRequestedAt, when needsReviewDispatch is evaluated and reconcileUatGenerations runs with the member still in the ready set, then the predicate returns false and the reconciler invalidates no generation

Given the same generation with the member absent from the ready set, when reconcileUatGenerations runs, then it invalidates the generation with a 'left the ready queue' reason — proving the assertion in ac1 is sensitive

Reference PAN-3083 as the incident where an unconsumed intent re-dispatched passed+ready issues and invalidated UAT generations.
